Question B-001-011-006.

Why the correct answer is right: Disaster relief transmissions are allowed when normal communication systems are overloaded, damaged, or disrupted and essential needs must be met.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Never, only official emergency stations may transmit in a disaster": The rule allows disaster-relief transmissions when normal systems are overloaded, damaged, or disrupted; it is broader than designated emergency stations only.
- sourceIndex 2: "When normal communication systems are working but are not convenient": Inconvenient but working normal systems do not meet the overloaded, damaged, or disrupted condition.
- sourceIndex 3: "Only when the local emergency net is activated": A local net activation may organize traffic, but the disaster-relief condition is the state of normal communication systems.
